risks.note: Non-availability of key raw materials may impact operations, and price fluctuations in polymers, wood, oils, chemicals and pigments may raise production costs and compress margins. Mitigated through long-term supplier relationships, periodic price reviews, strategic inventory buffers, multi-supplier sourcing for critical inputs and backward integration in selected inputs such as wood processing.
risks.risk: Raw material availability and price volatility

risks.note: Operations depend on timely availability of raw and packaging materials; geopolitical tensions, trade restrictions, changes in import/export regulations, global supply chain disruptions and swings in freight and logistics costs can disrupt procurement, raise operating costs and hit export volumes to affected countries. BRSR flags the financial implication as negative. Managed via buffer stock for critical inputs, multi-regional sourcing, extended vendor agreements, a varied base of logistics providers and backup shipping procedures.
risks.risk: Supply chain disruption, trade restrictions and logistics cost inflation

risks.note: Competitive intensity may create pricing pressure and erode market share and profitability. Countered through operational efficiency and cost competitiveness, product innovation, portfolio diversification, strategic partnerships and regular monitoring of market trends.
risks.risk: Intense competition from domestic and international players

risks.note: Variability in product quality, colour consistency or writing performance can damage customer experience, brand reputation and product acceptance - a direct risk for a branded consumer business. Addressed with stringent standards across sourcing, processing, manufacturing, packaging and distribution, dedicated QA/QC teams, defined SOPs and standardised testing, plus reduced dependence on third-party developers.

Operational disruptions or equipment failures may affect production efficiency, product quality and business continuity. Managed through operational controls, preventive maintenance systems and defined safety policies.

Infringement of trademarks or designs may dilute brand value and reduce consumer trust, a structural exposure for a company whose moat rests on brand equity. Managed by registering trademarks, designs and copyrights domestically and internationally, monitoring infringements and pursuing legal remedies with channel partners.
risks.risk: Brand protection and intellectual property infringement

risks.note: Employees and KMP are critical to delivering short- and long-term objectives; failure to retain, engage and manage talent could impact business sustainability and operational performance. Managed through training, mentorship, career development, performance feedback, ESOP benefits and diversity, equity and inclusion initiatives.
risks.risk: People risk - retention of employees and key managerial personnel

risks.note: Operations generate waste, primarily plastic waste, whose disposal is legally regulated; the Company states it is susceptible to fines or legal action in case of violation. Mitigated through a circular manufacturing approach reusing leftover polymers, graphite and calcium carbonate, reuse of packaging, water treatment and recycling, plastic waste handled through authorised recyclers under EPR regulations, hazardous waste through certified agencies and sawdust converted into briquettes.
